name: identity
title: Identity
description: One player, rendered: an avatar, a name, and whatever the host puts beside them. The three avatar cases are on `data-gs-avatar` as `image`, `fallback` and `none`, so a test asserts which one landed without hunting for an ``, and a player with no picture, or whose picture fails, gets a symbol and a hue hashed from their id, never a face or an initial. Signed out is a first-class state: pass `player={null}` and it renders the designed case, carrying `data-gs-anonymous`. Presence and `you` change the accessible name as well as the pixels. It renders identity and never performs authentication: no network call, no cookie, no token, no identity provider.
docs: Pass the adapter's `player`, or `null` before sign-in; both are supported renderings and the null one is what every identity surface shows first. `data-gs-anonymous` is your word that there is no player, never a check this component made and never a security boundary: hiding content behind it is client-side access control, which this library does not do. Pass `you` for the row belonging to the player holding the device, `presence` when you know whether they are here, and `avatar={false}` for a dense row that wants the name alone. Children render beside the name and stay announced, so a stat, a badge or a control can sit in the row. The avatar's shape comes from `--gs-shape-identity`, which the arcade theme sets to `circle`. Pass presentation="row" for the boxed player or opponent row specimen 3a draws, with `side` naming which; `you` implies the player's side.
